tagline: Mountain-ringed highland capital with cable cars
summary: Seat of government at about 3,600 m (El Alto airport at 4,000 m), spread down a canyon under Illimani. Loud, steep, chaotic and fascinating, with the best markets and the most tours in Bolivia.
things_to_do: Valle de la Luna and Chacaltaya day trips
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

summary: Small town at about 3,840 m on Lake Titicaca with a 17th-century basilica and the boats to Isla del Sol. Relaxed and backpacker-friendly, with trout on every menu; the Candelaria feast on 2 Feb brings dances and crowds.
things_to_do: Basilica of Our Lady of Copacabana
Grilled lake trout on the waterfront
Pedal boat or kayak on the lake
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Car-free Inca island on Lake Titicaca
summary: Rocky island with about 800 families, over 80 ruins, terraced hills and no cars or paved roads. Quiet village stays with big lake views; the north-south ridge walk is the draw.
things_to_do: Titi Qala sacred rock and Chinkana ruins
Sunrise and sunset from a Yumani guesthouse
Boat out to Isla de la Luna
hostel_price_note: Guesthouses USD 15-50 per night (bushop 2026). Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Warm green Yungas hill town above the jungle
summary: Small town at about 1,500 m, much warmer than La Paz, with fruit, coca and cloud-forest views. Slow, hammock-and-pool pace, mostly weekend visitors from La Paz.
things_to_do: Death Road finish and Yungas road views
Pool and hammock day at a hillside hostel
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Mining city and Carnaval capital, mostly a stopover
summary: Cold high-plains city at about 3,700 m that wakes up for the Carnaval de Oruro in February (UNESCO listed). The rest of the year it is a quiet transit point with few travellers.
things_to_do: Virgen del Socavon sanctuary and mirador
hostel_price_note: Very few hostels; accommodation fills and prices jump around Carnaval. Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Gateway to the world's biggest salt flat
summary: Dusty railway town at 3,650 m that exists to launch Salar de Uyuni tours. Dec to Feb is rainy season, when a thin water layer gives the famous mirror effect but roads and tours can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Salar de Uyuni 1-day or 3-day jeep tour
Mirror effect at sunrise and sunset in rainy season
Lagunas Colorada and Verde on multi-day tours
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Tourist sources quote dorm USD 10-18 in Uyuni (touristsecrets 2026).

tagline: Silver-mining city under Cerro Rico at 4,000 m
summary: One of the world's highest cities, built on the silver of Cerro Rico. Cold, atmospheric colonial centre with working-miner history; mine tours are the draw and are not for everyone.
things_to_do: Casa Nacional de Moneda mint museum
Santa Teresa convent and cathedral tower
Colonial streets around Plaza 10 de Noviembre
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: White colonial capital with a mild climate
summary: Constitutional capital at 2,800 m with whitewashed colonial buildings, good cafes and a student feel. Milder and calmer than La Paz; popular for Spanish classes and long stays.
things_to_do: Plaza 25 de Mayo and Casa de la Libertad
Mirador de la Recoleta at sunset
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. City dorm range USD 6-14 (bushop 2026).

tagline: Red-rock cowboy town in the far south
summary: High-desert town at about 2,850 m among red canyons and cacti, tied to the Butch Cassidy legend. Quiet and frontier-like, the cheaper and calmer start for a 3-4 day Salar tour.
things_to_do: Horseback ride through Quebrada Palala and Valle de los Machos
Canyon del Inca and Puerta del Diablo
Butch Cassidy trail and San Vicente
4x4 start of the Salar de Uyuni tour (3 to 4 days)
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Local-feeling valley city known for food
summary: Warm valley city at 2,550 m with a mild climate and Bolivia's best eating scene. Few tourists, big markets and a laid-back university-town pace.
things_to_do: Cristo de la Concordia hilltop statue
Lunch at a picanteria (silpancho, pique macho)
Day trip to Tarata or Incallajta ruins
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

summary: Hot, flat and modern, Bolivia's biggest city and a trade hub. Mostly a practical stop with a pleasant colonial plaza, good restaurants and the base for Samaipata and the Jesuit missions.
things_to_do: Plaza 24 de Septiembre and the cathedral tower
Biocentro Guembe butterfly and orchid park
Lowland cooking and cafes around Equipetrol
Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos day tour
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Laid-back expat and backpacker valley town
summary: Small town at about 1,650 m in the foothills near Amboro park with a big foreign-resident scene. Cafes, hammocks and cloud-forest walks, and the base for the pre-Inca El Fuerte site.
things_to_do: El Fuerte de Samaipata carved rock ruins (UNESCO)
Amboro National Park waterfalls and tree ferns
Cafe and bakery lunches on the plaza
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. One source quoted Hostel Serena dorms from GBP 9.5 and privates from GBP 29 (alongdustyroads, 2025); not converted to DKK.

tagline: Amazon gateway on the Beni River
summary: Hot, humid river town where the Andes drop into the lowlands. Gateway for Madidi jungle lodges and the Pampas wildlife tours; Dec to Feb is rainy season so trails and flights can be disrupted.
things_to_do: Madidi National Park jungle lodge stay
Pampas boat tour with caiman, capybara and pink dolphins
Beni River sunset and the ferry to San Buenaventura
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

summary: Large, walkable-in-parts city with a grand colonial centre, big food and craft-market culture and a lively student and art scene. Dec to Feb is dry and sunny.
things_to_do: Centro Historico: cathedral, Plaza de Armas, Hospicio Cabanas
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null.

tagline: Agave landscape town and tequila heartland
summary: UNESCO-listed agave landscape an hour from Guadalajara, built around distilleries. Pretty plaza and tasting rooms; most visitors come as a day trip.
things_to_do: Tequila Express or Jose Cuervo Express train
Plaza and parish of Santiago Apostol
hostel_price_note: No hostels found; most visitors day-trip from Guadalajara. Prices null.

summary: Steep hillside city of tunnels, plazas and pastel houses, UNESCO listed. Student energy, callejoneadas and museums in a small walkable centre.
things_to_do: Alley of the Kiss and Teatro Juarez
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Hostelz Mexico average: no figure for Guanajuato.

summary: Mexico's biggest lake, with Chapala town and Ajijic's cobbled artsy village, a large North American expat community. Very calm; the lake is not a swimming draw.
things_to_do: Scorpion Island and Mezcala boat trip
hostel_price_note: Only one hostel listed (dorm 'from MX$83' on Hostelz, not converted). Hotels and Airbnbs dominate.

tagline: Pacific resort town with cobbled old centre
summary: Beach and party town on Banderas Bay with a malecon, Zona Romantica and jungle-backed beaches. Dec to Feb is peak season with humpback whales and high prices.
things_to_do: Zona Romantica and Playa Los Muertos
hostel_price_note: Per-hostel nightly prices not published without dates; Hostelz/Hostelworld 'from' prices judged unreliable, so null. Peak season dorm prices run above the average.
